verdict.rationale: Gemini's docs say users can upload photos to get answers and insights, and on Android can ask for help with what's on the screen, so the core image-sharing and interpretation capability exists. Accuracy is unproven and mixed: a hands-on test found Gemini 3 still misidentified a photoshopped five-legged dog, though it did notice the fifth leg. missing for 10: first-party evidence that interpretation is accurate, explicit documentation of uploading screenshots (as opposed to live on-screen help), and independent corroboration of reliable image understanding without notable misreads.

support.subject: As a knowledge-worker, I can share screenshots and photos and have the assistant accurately interpret what is in them

citations.quote: You can upload documents, spreadsheets, notebooks, photos, videos, and more to Gemini Apps to get answers, summaries, and insights about your content.
On Android, say “Hey Google” to ask Gemini for help with what’s on your screen
Gemini 3 however, while still failing, at least recognized the 5th leg
